propositions: A check that asserts the absence of a condition (via grep, empty collection, or negation) derived from subprocess/file/network output cannot distinguish its PASS result from the producer never having run, crashed, or emitted nothing.
A check that produces a confident FAIL result due to a broken instrument (wrong input, self-match, silent miss) is indistinguishable from an actual failure of the condition being verified.

The fail-open oracle antipattern (inability to distinguish any definite result from producer failure) appears in both test-code population (nine instances: signal-killed child, re-derived convergence, colorized grep, truncated log, unchecked returncode, silent lookup miss, environ scan skip, pgrep self-match) and shipped-code population (gate scripts, health checks, membership tests).

Producer-liveness detection language must be added to existing `tests` criterion (test-oracle population) and `error-handling` criterion (shipped-code population) rather than as a new criterion, with shared litmus: name every world in which the check produces its definite result; if producer-never-ran/emitted-nothing is among them, the check cannot distinguish its verdict from its own failure.

The fail-open pattern has a mirror (false alarm on total absence when instrument failed): the criterion language must cover both PASS and FAIL false verdicts, and both absence assertions and presence-verification checks.
